articles.title: Steph Curry, Draymond's Reaction to Being Benched to Start Warriors' OT vs. Magic Revealed by Kerr
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors stars Stephen Curry and Draymond Green were understandably perplexed when they were on the bench to start overtime in Saturday's 126-119 win over the Orlando Magic.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors stars Stephen Curry and Draymond Green were understandably perplexed when they were on the bench to start overtime in Saturday's 126-119 win over the Orlando Magic.

"Steph and Dray weren't thrilled at first when I told them what we were going to do," coach Steve Kerr said, per The Athletic's Jason Jones . "But they understood and those guys gave us a four-point lead and really played well and set the table for Steph and Dray to come back and close the game."

Curry and Green entered with 3:48 remaining in overtime and Golden State up by two points. The Magic regained the lead, only for Curry to sink a finger roll and get fouled, knocking down the free throw. The Warriors didn't trail for the final 1:38.

The two franchise stalwarts acknowledged their initial annoyance at Kerr's strategy.

"And obviously me and Draymond are gonna have a reaction to that because we're competitors and wanna be out there," Curry said. "And the conversation and the energy was more frustration for us, not doubt in the unit that was going out there. And we wanted to make sure they knew that because they've been playing well all year."

Green pushed back in the moment before finally coming around.

"Eventually we're like, 'Cool. Come on, fellas, y'all got it,'" he said. "'We believe in y'all. We wanna play, but we believe in y'all.'"

Managing the workloads of Curry and Green is a season-long task. Giving them a brief rest may not mean much on a given night. All of those minutes they were on the bench can add up over an 82-game season.

Kerr may have also savored the opportunity to put his younger players in a difficult situation and get them that experience. Rookie forward Yaxel Lendeborg played all of overtime and scored seven points during the extra period.

Curry and Green can't carry the Warriors like they once did. They need the supporting cast to step up to have any hope of achieving a deep playoff run.

Kerr knows this as well and will coach appropriately depending on the situation.

articles.title: Bronny James' Lakers Status Updated After Breakout Game in NBA G League Win
articles.summary: Bronny James impressed in the G-League, and now he is returning to the Los Angeles Lakers.
articles.body:
Bronny James impressed in the G-League, and now he is returning to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Ayomide Adeduyite of Athlon Sports noted the Lakers recalled James and Cameron Carr ahead of their four-game road trip that starts Sunday against the Detroit Pistons and features games against the Atlanta Hawks, Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns.

Los Angeles previously sent them to the Coachella Valley Lakers, and James thrived during the G-League's team against the Salt Lake City Stars with 22 points, seven assists and five rebounds in a 104-98 win.

He also said, "It's good to be in a new environment."

James, who is the son of the legendary LeBron James, was buried in the Lakers' rotation in the early portion of the season. While it was just a brief appearance at the G-League, it was also an opportunity for the 22-year-old to get some playing time instead of just sitting on the end of the team's bench.

"The messaging was very simple," Lakers head coach JJ Redick said, per Benjamin Royer of the Orange County Register . "It's just: you guys need reps and you guys need to play."

James is averaging just 2.4 minutes per game in his five appearances for the Lakers this season.

Los Angeles also hasn't needed him much, as it is off to an excellent 8-2 start with Luka Dončić leading the way as an early MVP candidate. Dončić is averaging a stunning 40.1 points per game on the campaign and dropped 53 in Friday's win over the Portland Trail Blazers.

It was his fourth straight game with at least 40 points and second game of the season with more than 50.

There is no doubt the Lakers are Dončić's team at this point, but James will look to carve out a role in the rotation following his appearance in the G-League.

articles.title: Tyler Kolek Addresses Taylor Swift 'Fakest' Knicks Fan Comment, Covers Song in New Viral Video
articles.summary: After feeling the wrath of the Swifties, New York Knicks guard Tyler Kolek is walking back his comments about Taylor Swift.
articles.body:
After feeling the wrath of the Swifties, New York Knicks guard Tyler Kolek is walking back his comments about Taylor Swift.

In a video on the NBA 2K League TikTok account , Kolek named Swift as the "fakest" celebrity Knicks fan and said her support of the team during its championship run was "a little performative." He now admits that he was unaware of her level of fandom.

"Obviously with everything (going on), people have been going back and sending me all the stuff about her going to the games," Kolek said Saturday after the Knicks' 109-97 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers, per The Athletic's Fred Katz . "And she was actually wearing a 13 jersey (in one picture). Probably Joakim Noah back in the day with Carmelo (Anthony). So, I wasn't up to date on my Taylor Swift Knicks fandom, so that's on me."

Kolek's comments prompted the Knicks to release a statement addressing the matter, saying, "Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization."

Katz noted that the Knicks played "blasted Swift's songs in the locker room" after Friday's practice and Saturday's win, playing "Shake It Off," then "You Belong With Me."

"(The video) was everywhere. Everybody saw it," Kolek said. "But it is what it is. For me, it's just a question that was asked to me that maybe I answered in the wrong way. I take that on the chin. But I love her music. We were just playing it five minutes ago and I'm singing every word to every song. Nothing against her at all."

Kolek is hoping to avoid further conflict with the Swifties, as he is one of them himself.

"I love her music. I probably know more songs than anybody else in the locker room," he said. "I just misspoke."

articles.title: Philip Rivers finalizing agreement to return to NC State as Wolfpack’s new head coach in remarkable move
articles.summary: Philip Rivers had already begun assembling a coaching staff before formally accepting the NC State job, sources say. His son Gunner enrolls in January.
articles.body: After N.C. State officials made the trek to Fairhope, Alabama earlier this week to formally meet with Philip Rivers, the former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback appears to be set to take the head coaching position at his alma mater. The two sides are finalizing an agreement that is expected to be hammered out over the next 24 hours, sources told OutKick. The board of trustees at N.C. State have a meeting this coming week to approve the contract. Conversations about Rivers taking the job in Raleigh had picked up after the school announced that Dave Doeren had been fired nearly two weeks ago. Following a series of informal discussions with major donors about what it would take to make N.C. State competitive in the current era of college athletics, several Wolfpack boosters put a plan in motion to provide Rivers with the resources needed to hit the ground running. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE By the end of the week, all that was needed was pen to paper for the NC State alum. But first, Rivers was going to finish his job as head coach of St. Michael Catholic in the Alabama high school football playoffs. His season came to an end on Friday night in Fairhope, as they lost in the opening round. NC State gave Rivers the space needed to coach, now it's onto Raleigh According to multiple sources, Rivers had already begun putting together a coaching and front office staff for when he formally accepted the job offer and signed a contract. On Friday night, Rivers was coaching St. Michael Catholic in their Alabama high school playoff game, where his son Gunner also plays. In addition to the intrigue of coaching for the first time in college, Gunner is also committed to NC State and will enroll in January to start his own collegiate career. One of the biggest points of emphasis for Rivers taking the job in Raleigh was that he would be given enough money to work with for a veteran coaching staff, given that this will be his first college job. Sources tell OutKick that one of his contract asks was that he be given a big enough pool of money to attract assistant coaches with college experience that would be open to making a move to Raleigh. Also, having the NIL resources outside of the revenue-sharing that schools participate in was a key part of negotiations for NC State athletic director Boo Corrigan landing the former NFL quarterback. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT From a fan perspective, it's obvious that the Wolfpack would be making a hire that would excite the base, and more importantly help sell tickets and also lead to an influx of donations needed to help fund rosters in the future. Offering Philip Rivers the NC State job was a risk worth taking This is seen as a win-win for both sides, given that this would obviously be an interesting splash around college football, especially in recruiting players who are familiar with the new head coach. But there is also the obvious fact that players are going to go where the money leads them, though that's clearly not the case for every player. Still, putting together a formidable roster that can compete in the ACC and subsequently for a spot in the upcoming expanded College Football Playoff is key to making sure this hire doesn’t turn into a dud over the next few years. NICK SABAN SPEAKS TRUTH ON CFP EXPANSION: ‘THERE’S NOT 24 TEAMS’ THAT CAN WIN A NATIONAL TITLE, BUT MONEY WINS We have seen countless coordinators in the college ranks receive their first shot at a head coaching job and watch it turn into chaos; just look at what is taking place with Tosh Lupoi at Cal this season, where general manager Ron Rivera is already sounding the alarms. But, for a high school coach to be given an opportunity to start their collegiate career at the top, and especially at a school like NC State, goes to show you how much Wolfpack officials think about Rivers. Now, the donors who have promised Rivers with the funds needed to compete will be tasked with making sure he can attack the transfer portal to add players to this NC State roster so that he can hit the ground running for the 2027 season. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP This will be an interesting situation to watch unfold over the next few months, with NC State fans expecting this team to once again start competing for ACC titles on a yearly basis. Welcome to college football, Philip Rivers.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Injury Update, Latest on Lakers Star's Status amid Scoring Streak
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers will be without star Luka Dončić for Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons because of lower back tightness.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers will be without star Luka Dončić for Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons because of lower back tightness.

Dončić's health was a major storyline for the 2025-26 Lakers, as injuries forced him to miss the end of the regular season and the team's playoff win over the Houston Rockets and loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Defeating the Thunder would have been a daunting task even with a healthy Dončić, but the Lakers had no chance without him.

That is because he is one of the best players in the entire league with a resume that includes a Western Conference Finals MVP, two scoring titles, a Rookie of the Year, six All-NBA selections and six All-Star nods.

He led the league in scoring last season while averaging 33.5 points, 8.3 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game and shooting 47.6 percent from the field and 36.6 percent from deep.

Dončić became even more important for the Lakers ahead of the 2026-27 campaign when LeBron James departed in free agency and signed with the Philadelphia 76ers. It was a further signal that the Purple and Gold were Dončić's team moving forward.

He has delivered in the early going this season and is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists through his first nine games.

Dončić has scored 40 or more points in four consecutive games.

If he is sidelined by this latest setback beyond just Sunday's game, Los Angeles will likely rely even more on Austin Reaves to carry the offense from the perimeter. Look for Collin Sexton to see even more playing time as well as the team looks to tread water during the star's absence.

Still, the only way the Lakers are going to realistically compete with the top teams in the Western Conference is with a healthy Dončić.

articles.title: Luka Dončić sidelined for Lakers-Pistons game due to back tightness
articles.summary: The Lakers announced his status hours before Sunday's 6 p.m. ET tip. He entered Sunday listed as questionable.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have downgraded Luka Dončić to out for Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons due to lower back tightness.

The Lakers announced his status hours before Sunday's scheduled 6 p.m. ET tip in Detroit. He entered Sunday listed as questionable. It's not clear if the injury will sideline Dončić for multiple games.

Sunday's game against the Pistons is the first of a back-to-back. The Lakers will visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday.

A six-time All-NBA selection, Dončić is off to a sensational start to the season. Through nine games, Dončić is the NBA's leading scorer with averages of 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game while shooting 49.8% from the field and 41.9% on 13.8 3-point attempts per game.

The Lakers are off to an 8-2 start with Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler anchoring the lineup in the first season since the departure of LeBron James. Dončić is playing like an MVP candidate as the primary driver behind the Lakers' strong start. The Lakers are certainly hoping that his back injury isn't one that will linger.

articles.title: Kon Knueppel Injury Updates, Latest Timeline on Hornets Star After Getting Hurt in Season Debut

articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets forward Kon Knueppel will miss at least four weeks with a hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday:

Knueppel suffered the injury on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets, a setback after returning from his prior injury. He lasted only six minutes in his season debut before being ruled out with "leg soreness," the team announced:

He had just three points before exiting in the first quarter.

Knueppel had been sidelined by a hamstring strain he suffered during offseason workouts in September. The injury forced the 21-year-old to miss the entire preseason and all eight of Charlotte's games to the start of the 2026-27 season.

The latest setback is another disappointment for a team that has struggled to find its footing so far this season. After winning three of their first four games, the Hornets lost four consecutive games heading into their matchup against Brooklyn and ranked dead last in scoring offense.

The team's struggles can partially be explained by the absence of Knueppel and starting guard Coby White. Knueppel at full strength could help Charlotte get its season back on track, although there are now more questions about his health.

Knueppel was selected with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft and dazzled during his rookie campaign. He earned NBA All-Rookie First Team honors and finished second in NBA Rookie of the Year voting behind Cooper Flagg. Knueppel finished the season with 273 made three-pointers, making him the first rookie to lead the league in three-pointers made in NBA history.

articles.title: El Madrid pulveriza al UCAM Murcia en seis minutos
articles.standfirst: Un parcial de 15-0 en el arranque del último cuarto entierra las opciones murcianas
articles.summary: Un parcial de 15-0 en el arranque del último cuarto entierra las opciones murcianas
articles.body: El Real Madrid continúa perdiendo jugadores, pero sigue invicto en la Liga Endesa. Chuma Okeke fue la última baja de los blancos por problemas físicos, pero ni siquiera eso impidió que los blancos minimizaran al UCAM Murcia, 90-71, con un parcial de 15-0 en seis minutos en el arranque del último cuarto para ganar con más comodidad un partido que se presentaba mucho más complicado. Por muy bien que juegues en los tres primeros cuartos, por mucho que te aferres al partido e incluso que metas algo de miedo (58-55 a 1:41 para el final del tercer cuarto), si te pasas casi seis minutos del último periodo sin anotar, estás muerto. Eso el pasó al UCAM Murcia que aguantó varias veces los chaparrones del Madrid para, con un parcial de 0-7, colocarse a esos tres puntos muy cerca del final del tercer acto y mantener el partido muy vivo. Pero tras el comienzo del último periodo, colapso completo del Murcia ante un Madrid que empezó a jugar a placer y trató de paliar al final su discreto partido en porcentajes. Okeke se bajó del barco a última hora por problemas físicos que habrá que ver hasta dónde llegan. Su lugar en el equipo lo ocupó el júnior Pablo Mera que a sus 16 años pudo debutar en la Liga Endesa a 1:22 para el final y con el partido decidido (84-65) y que, espoleado por el público se jugó y acertó con un triple. Mera incluso salió a jugar por delante de Nick Smith que ya no cuenta para Pedro Martínez. A pesar de la baja de Okeke y las de otros muchos jugadores (Campazzo, Maledon, Jantunen, además de Garuba y Deck), los blancos supieron mantener su ritmo de juego habitual sin un destacado especialmente. Aunque Damian Jones siguió ganando crédito entre los favoritos de la afición blanca gracias a su 3/4 en triples, máxima fiabilidad desde el arco, y un gran mate. Jones acabó con 13 puntos, aunque fue Pradilla, en un buen partido, el mejor anotador del Madrid con 15 puntos. Abalde acabó con 12 puntos y Feliz se fue con 11. El equipo de Pedro Martínez dominó los dos primeros cuartos. El primero para irse con una mínima ventaja, 22-20, y el segundo para establecer un ligera diferencia cuando los dos equipos se iban a los vestuarios, 47-39. Ahí ya se había visto que el Murcia proponía un partido incómodo y que el Madrid no estaba en su mejor día en cuanto a efectividad anotadora. Sito Alonso se quejó al final del partido de que, a pesar del trabajo defensivo durante todo el choque, los blancos acabaron anotando 90 puntos. Fue porque el Murcia desapareció en el arranque del tercer cuarto hasta el punto de que, cuando restaban 3:41 para el final del partido, la máxima ventaja blanca alcanzó los 25 puntos (82-57). El Madrid facturó ante el UCAM Murcia su séptimo triunfo en siete partidos en la Liga Endesa. Es el único equipo que aún no ha perdido en el campeonato doméstico, clasificación que domina con 147 puntos a favor, casi el doble que el segundo (Valencia, 78).

articles.title: NBA Rumor: Why Trading Naz Reid For Scoot Henderson Makes Zero Sense For Charlotte
articles.summary: Social media speculation moves fast across the league, and a recent NBA rumor floating a trade between the Portland Trail Blazers and the Charlotte Hornets h...
articles.body:
Social media speculation moves fast across the league, and a recent NBA rumor floating a trade between the Portland Trail Blazers and the Charlotte Hornets has generated plenty of online chatter. The proposed framework features Portland sending fourth-year guard Scoot Henderson , draft capital centered on the Orlando Magic's 2028 first-round pick, and salary filler to Charlotte in exchange for Naz Reid.

On the surface, it is easy to see why observers might connect those dots. Charlotte's perimeter depth is severely tested, secondary guard options are sidelined, and the backcourt is taking nightly beatings. However, while acquiring a high-lottery guard and a future draft pick sounds enticing on a broadcast, evaluating Charlotte's actual timeline and roster makeup reveals why this trade makes zero sense.

Scoot Henderson Does Not Solve Charlotte's Floor-Spacing Reality

The main issue with bringing in Henderson isn't about belittling his talent—it comes down to fit on a Hornets roster that is missing LaMelo Ball's offense .

Henderson possesses raw downhill athleticism, but he remains a high-variance guard who needs high usage to operate while still trying to establish consistent perimeter shooting.

Through his early NBA career, Henderson has struggled with three-point efficiency and decision-making in high-leverage possessions. Charlotte's offense is already drowning in heavy turnover numbers. Adding another non-spacing ball-handler who turns the ball over at a high rate doesn't fix Charlotte's half-court execution; it simply compounds the mess.

Furthermore, Henderson's point-of-attack defense hasn't reached a level where he can hold up without heavy backline support. Swapping a functional piece for a developing guard who adds more spacing friction to the floor doesn't help what Charles Lee is trying to establish.

Trading Reid creates an immediate, unnecessary hole in Charlotte's frontcourt. Reid isn't saving this franchise, but he is a productive, modern big who can shoot from deep, handle in secondary actions, and play multiple frontcourt spots. If Charlotte ships Reid to Portland, the squad is left without a single starter-level power forward capable of stretching defenses and making plays off the bounce.

Also, Reid gives Charlotte the ability to run versatile big-man pairings or slide into standalone center looks. Stripping the frontcourt of one of its floor-spacing options just to hoard more guard depth destroys what little functional structure this offense has.

Draft Assets Don't Fix The Current Timeline

Proponents of the rumor highlight Portland, including the Magic's 2028 first-round pick, as the key draft sweetener to get a deal done. Future draft picks are always useful, but a distant 2028 first-round pick does nothing for Charlotte's immediate day-to-day development.

Jeff Peterson made the franchise's direction clear when he traded away Ball in the offseason and preached patience for a long-term build. Charlotte knows this season is going to be rough. But taking on a reclamation project in Henderson while stripping the roster of frontcourt spacing for a distant draft pick isn't rebuilding—it's just accumulating random parts without a blueprint.

It is easy to get reactive when injuries pile up, and the losses get ugly. Between Brandon Miller exiting with a groin injury , Kon Knueppel 's hamstring strain, and secondary guard absences, the backcourt looks paper-thin. However, panicking into a trade for a guard who doesn't fit the floor isn't the answer.

This season was always going to be about taking hits and establishing habits. Charlotte isn't fighting for a playoff spot, and trading away solid frontcourt pieces for a high-turnover guard and distant picks won't speed up the timeline.

While Portland would gladly take Reid's frontcourt versatility off Charlotte's hands, the Hornets have no reason to bite. Henderson's game doesn't fix Charlotte's half-court flaws, a 2028 pick doesn't replace starter-level frontcourt minutes, and losing Reid leaves the roster completely empty at power forward.

Charlotte needs to take its lumps, stay patient, and ignore trade frameworks that make a bad situation worse.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum closeness stood out to Danilo Gallinari in time with Celtics
articles.summary: Despite their recent furor, the ties between the two champion Celtics forwards were actually complimentary, if anything.
articles.body:
MEXICO CITY - Boston Celtics forward alum Danilo Gallinari has felt the heat of being on the wrong end of a clickbait narrative not long ago after comments about his health in Boston were taken out of context. Ironically, when he was with the Celtics, he managed to mostly avoid the ire of such framing despite injuring himself in FIBA play before the start of his tenure.

"As far as media coverage, I didn't play, unfortunately, that season in Boston, so I couldn't really experience the media coverage," Gallinari told the Celtics Wire as the Boston alum paid a visit to the 2026 NBA Mexico Game this past Thursday (Nov 5), sounding almost as if he regretted having not been in such a fight.

However, he did have a privileged view of two Celtics teammates who often found themselves in similar narratives despite the success on the court they found together. Those teammates – Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown – have seen new life breathed into those takes after the trade of Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer, though there may be some substance to them, at least now. But from where Gallinari could see, their connection was complimentary, if anything. "The relationship that I saw was amazing because they were spending a lot of time together," he explained.

"They were playing so much one-on-one together every single day, which is something that I've never seen from two All-Stars in a team," recalled Gallinari. "(When) I was the star of the team, I didn't play that much 1-on-1 with the other stars of the team."

"And I haven't seen that dynamic in too many teams that I've played in," added the Sant'Angelo Lodigiano native. "So it was great to see that. Once I saw that, I was like, 'Well, your two best players, your two stars, have that relationship on the court. We have a chance to win the championship'. So for me, it was great to see how they were handling themselves on the court."

We may never know if something happened between the two since that campaign falling between their 2022 and 2024 NBA Finals appearances, a liminal campaign that will remain part of the ties between these three Boston forward alumni.

But if something did cause Brown and Tatum to have fallen out afterward, the seeds of it had not yet begun to produce visible growth during the time Gallinari was around them.

articles.title: Sarah Strong explodes with career-high 39 points to lead No. 2 UConn over No. 10 Iowa
articles.summary: In the Huskies' second ranked matchup of the week, Strong showed up big in the 91-79 win over the Hawkeyes.
articles.body:
After finishing last season as the consensus player of the year , Sarah Strong is picking up where she left off.

In a top-10 matchup between No. 2 UConn and No. 10 Iowa, the junior Huskies forward exploded for 39 points on the way to a confident 91-79 win over the Hawkeyes. The number surpassed Strong's own career high by a significant margin.

Strong went 15-for-26 from the field, sinking five 3-pointers while also tallying 10 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 blocks. She played 37 minutes in the matchup, and surpassed her previous career-high (29) halfway through the third quarter.

The 39-point score line is the most scored by a UConn player against a top-10 team since 2000, per ESPN . Strong also becomes the fourth Division I player to ever hit that state line — 35-plus points, 10-plus rebounds and 5-plus 3-pointers — against a top 10 team in the 2000s, per ESPN.

Alongside Strong's dominant performance, sophomore forward Blanca Quiñonez pitched in 21 points off the bench, going 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Hawkeyes guard Chazadi "Chit-Chat" Wright led Iowa in points with a 23-point, 5-assist performance.

Unlike some other Power Four programs, UConn has front-loaded its schedule with ranked opponents, before starting (easier) Big East play next month. Before Sunday's game against No. 10 Iowa, the Huskies played No. 5 Michigan on Thursday, a game that ended in a Wolverines upset .

Upcoming matchups include No. 18 Ohio State and No. 7 Louisville next week, No. 1 South Carolina and No. 4 Duke later this month, and No. 13 Notre Dame and No. 9 LSU in December. (All of those rankings, including UConn's No. 2, are likely to change when the latest AP poll comes out on Monday.)

And of course there's LeBron James, tying it all together:

For all of Philly's individual talent, however, they haven't played selfishly. On Sunday the Sixers had 30 assists and just nine turnovers, crashed the boards hard (54-42 advantage) and continue to turn defense into easy buckets in transition.

The half-court offense is a work in progress, as expected. But the Sixers are doing the little things needed to win, and it's not as though they've had a cakewalk of a schedule thus far (4-2 record against the New York Knicks, Cleveland Cavaliers and Detroit Pistons).

They'll be tested again on Tuesday in a matchup against Brown's former team, the Boston Celtics. There should be a bit of spice to that one.

articles.title: Los Sixers asaltan Chicago y firman su mejor arranque en 26 años
articles.standfirst: Los titulares de Philly anotaron 109 puntos
articles.summary: Los titulares de Philly anotaron 109 puntos
articles.body: Con 109 de los 127 puntos anotados por los titulares, los Philadelphia 76ers se llevaron el triunfo del United Center al ganar a los Chicago Bulls, 121-127. A pesar de que se medían el líder del Este y uno de los colistas, los Bulls llevaron al límite a los Sixers y sólo los tiros libres de Jaylen Brown en los segundos finales pudieron asegurar el noveno triunfo en 11 partidos de Philly, su mejor comienzo tras 11 partidos desde 2000-01. Los Bulls, por su parte, sólo suman un triunfo y un 0-3 ante su público en un horrible arranque de temporada. El 1-8 iguala el peor arranque tras nueve partidos de su historia. Durante muchos minutos a los Sixers los sostuvo LeBron James, mejor anotador del equipo al descanso con 16 puntos. Acabó con 22 y superado por los dos mejores artilleros de Philly, Brown, 29, en su segundo mejor partido anotador desde que llegó, y Maxey, 27 con un gran 9/16 en tiros de campo. Embiid, con un doble-doble de 18 puntos y 10 rebotes y Edgecombe, 13 puntos, completaron los 109 puntos logrados entre los titulares. Chicago estuvo a mejor nivel de lo que indica ese solitario triunfo con 19 puntos de Buzelis, y una enorme mate al final, y Giddey y 18 de Caleb Wilson. Los Bulls cedieron en los dos primeros cuartos, 33-34 y 28-34, ganaron el tercero 32-31 y empataron el cuarto, 28-28. Aunque en el tramo final los Sixers parecían tener el partido controlado en un par de ocasiones, los Bulls se las arreglaron para mantener el partido vivo hasta el final. A 6:07 Philly se escapó, 104-113 con buenos minutos de Maxey, pero un 6-0 en un minuto comprimió el marcador (110-113 a 5:03). Otro arreón de los Sixers, 116-123 con triple de Maxey y LeBron jugando como base, parecía decisivo a 2:05, pero de nuevo los Bulls se pegaron, 120-123, con un matazo de Buzelis a 1:03. En ese último minuto, Brown fue decisivo con dos rebotes ofensivos, dos faltas provocadas y cuatro tiros libres sin fallo que abrocharon el triunfo de Philadelphia. LeBron James, con los 22 puntos anotados en su partido 70 ante Chicago, se convirtió en el jugador que más puntos ha anotado a los Bulls en la historia de la NBA. El de los Sixers está ahora en 1.902 superando a Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (1.895) y dejando atrás a Dominique Wilkins (1.784), Isiah Thomas (1.431) y Dave Bing (1.416).

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Reveals If He'll Talk to Jayson Tatum Prior to 1st Celtics vs. 76ers Game Since Trade
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown doesn't seem interested in chopping it up with Jayson Tatum ahead of Tuesday's matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics, the first regular-season meeting between the teams since Brown was traded to Philly over the summer.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown doesn't seem interested in chopping it up with Jayson Tatum ahead of Tuesday's matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics, the first regular-season meeting between the teams since Brown was traded to Philly over the summer.

"There's nothing to talk about," he told reporters Sunday. "I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side. Playing basketball, both of us are trying to win. So there's nothing to talk about. Check the ball out.

Brown and Tatum have offered far different perspectives regarding Brown's trade this summer from the Celtics to the Sixers, culminating in Brown saying that there wasn't any beef between the two men but "there might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. He should stay ready at all times."

He also said that Tatum has "a great PR team."

Tatum has also said there was no beef, though he wasn't the player who was traded.

"I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum told reporters in late October. "The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we've grown together, right?"

Brown's traded in June—the Sixers sent Paul George, two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round picks (2028, 2030) to Boston to land the 30-year-old star—sent shockwaves throughout the NBA. Tatum and Brown had won a title together and were both in their prime, calling into question whether the partnership between the duo had started to splinter.

Regardless, it had something of a domino effect, with LeBron James later noting that part of the reason he joined the Sixers was the acquisition of Brown. Those Sixers are now 9-2 on the season and Brown is finding his groove with his new team, averaging 22.3 points per contest.

Tuesday's reunion between Brown and Tatum obviously is going to attract plenty of attention. But Brown didn't offer any insight into whether he's feeling extra motivation to stick it to his former teammate on Sunday.

articles.title: Siena women's basketball loses in return to MVP Arena
articles.summary: Sophomore guard Francesca Schiro had 30 points for the Saints, who lost their second straight game to fall to 1-2.
articles.body:
ALBANY - In the return of Siena women's basketball to MVP Arena after a four-year absence, visiting Binghamton was the team that looked more comfortable in the building - especially inside the 3-point line.

Bearcats forward Kendall Bennett had 27 points and 13 rebounds in a 79-73 victory over the Saints on Sunday in the America East-Metro Basketball Challenge.

Sophomore guard Francesca Schiro had 30 points for the Saints, who lost their second straight game to fall to 1-2.

"They continued to go to No. 4 (Bennett), and it took us too long to decide that we weren't going to let her be effective anymore," Siena coach Terry Primm said. "Once we did, I don't know if she touched the ball much down the stretch. But we've just got to play with a little more force. We've got to believe in what we're doing together. We can't separate and do it as individuals."

Binghamton outscored Siena 25-8 at the foul line and 42-26 in the paint, more than offsetting Siena's edge behind the 3-point line. The Saints shot 11-for-28 from beyond the arc, compared to the Bearcats' 2-for-11.

The Siena women played the second game of a doubleheader at MVP Arena with the Siena men, who beat Princeton 82-68 in the opener. Most of the men's crowd of 4,393 had filed out by the time the women's game began.

It was the Siena women's first time in the arena since a Nov. 16, 2022 loss to St. Bonaventure. They play their home games on campus at UHY Center.

"I mean, it was a cool experience," Schiro said. "I wish we had a couple more fans, but you know, we'll get there. But it was cool just to play in a big arena because it's always fun to do that. I enjoyed it."

Binghamton coach Mary (McKissack) Grimes entered familiar territory. As a Siena guard from 1999 to 2003, she played in MVP Arena many times in the regular season and the conference tournament.

"It definitely brought back some memories," Grimes said.

Of more immediate importance to Grimes was seeing her America East preseason favorite Bearcats (1-2) bounce back from lopsided losses to Coastal Athletic Association favorite Monmouth and three-time defending Metro champion Fairfield in their first two games.

"Talk about a buzzsaw," Grimes said. "But just being able to do what I asked, that was part of our film session is just we're doing things going rogue. We wanted to get it inside, whether we were driving or getting it to Kendall Bennett, and we were able to execute that game plan."

Binghamton's Bella Pucci added 22 points and five assists.

Siena led 62-59 before the Bearcats ripped off an 11-0 run to go ahead 70-62 with 3:31 to play.

Siena's Caydence Hadley finished with 12 points and a bandage on her chin.

"We just needed to be more physical to get the win," Hadley said. "At the end, it just kind of got away from us."

After scoring 43 points over her first two games, Siena guard Nicole Melious was held to five points on 2-of-13 shooting, including 1-for-9 on 3-pointers.

Siena will play Syracuse on Wednesday at JMA Wireless Dome.

articles.title: Lakers Beat Pistons with Luka Injured, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Cade, Reaves, Top Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have looked like championship contenders amid an MVP-caliber start from Luka Dončić, but the team got one of their biggest tests of the season so far, taking on the Detroit Pistons without their star.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have looked like championship contenders amid an MVP-caliber start from Luka Dončić, but the team got one of their biggest tests of the season so far, taking on the Detroit Pistons without their star.

The Lakers passed the test, beating the Pistons 121-116 despite being without Dončić.

Los Angeles was led by strong play from Austin Reaves, who helped make up for the absence of Dončić. Though Dončić has been the primary scorer for Los Angeles, Reaves has put together a solid year so far, coming into Sunday's game averaging 23.5 points per game. His 43 points on Sunday were a season high.

A slow night from Cade Cunningham also helped the Lakers out, as the star point guard couldn't get much going on offense. Daniss Jenkins was the only Piston who managed to find his rhythm, putting together a solid night off the bench.

The Lakers improved to 9-2 with the win, moving them into first place in the Western Conference, while the Pistons fell to 6-3.

Dončić has had an unbelievable start to the season, averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per game as he seeks both his first championship and his first MVP.

A back injury forced him to miss Sunday's game, but it's a good sign that the Lakers were able to get the job done without him.

articles.title: New Warriors Trade Rumors Update Team's Approach With Kristaps Porzingis After Health Update
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors remain "determined to trade" Kristaps Porziņģis, per NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer, even after the veteran center announced Friday that he was stepping away from basketball.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors remain "determined to trade" Kristaps Porziņģis, per NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer , even after the veteran center announced Friday that he was stepping away from basketball.

The Warriors would like to move Porziņģis "preferably" before Dec. 16 but would settle for any point ahead of the Feb. 11 NBA trade deadline, per that report.

It may be a tough needle to thread, however.

As Stein and Fischer noted, "Executives from three different rival teams told The Stein Line this week that they would insist on the Warriors adding some measure of draft capital to Porziņģis to part with a starting-caliber big man. ... The Warriors, league sources say, have not completely ruled out the prospect of adding some draft capital to Porziņģis' deal... but only for the proverbial right player. We're also told that the Warriors are determined to keep Moses Moody out of any in-season trade business if possible, believing that both Moody and [Jimmy] Butler can make successful returns from their respective knee injuries at some point in the second half of the season."

The Warriors are understandably trying to maximize whatever years Stephen Curry has left, and signing him to a two-year, $40 million contract in the offseason was supposed to aid in that effort. But the 31-year-old Porziņģis—who only played in 32 games last season between the Dubs and Atlanta Hawks—has struggled through injuries and medical issues throughout his career and doesn't seem inclined to play.

The Warriors have already been withholding his salary when he remains away from the team and is hoping to trade him as what would essentially be an expiring contract (he has a player option for next season). Perhaps for teams hoping to have less bloat on the books next summer, that may be an interesting proposition. For now, however, it seems as though the Warriors are going to have to pay to ditch him.

articles.title: Austin Reaves has sideline chat with Pistons fan, punctuates 43-point game in Lakers win with dagger 3 and wave goodbye
articles.summary: Reaves stepped up as Luka Dončić sat the first game of a back-to-back set with back tightness.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić missed Sunday's Los Angeles Lakers game against the Detroit Pistons due to lower back tightness.

The Lakers prevailed without him thanks to a big game from Austin Reaves, who also shared some words with a courtside fan in Detroit.

Reaves paced the Lakers with 43 points, 5 rebounds and 4 assists as the No. 1 option in Dončić's absence while shooting 14 of 27 from the field and 4 of 6 from 3. The effort anchored a 121-116 win that improved the Lakers' record to 9-2 and dropped the Pistons to 6-3.

Walker Kessler added 12 points, 16 rebounds, 4 assists and 3 blocks as the Lakers tied the Philadelphia 76ers for the best record in the NBA. Cade Cunningham posted 14 points, 8 assists and 4 turnovers while struggling from the field on a 6-of-15 shooting night in the losing effort.

During the game, Reaves shared words with a Pistons fan sitting courtside. It's not clear what was said, but they had a long talk during a break in action toward the end of the first half.

After he hit a late dagger 3, Reaves then waved goodbye to the fan.

Reaves played coy with reporters when asked about the interaction at his locker postgame.

"I don't know what you're talking about," Reaves said.

The night added to a strong start to the season from Reaves, who entered Sunday averaging 23.5 points, 4.7 assists and 3.2 rebounds per game while shooting 38.6% from 3.

The Lakers announced Dončić's status hours before Sunday's scheduled 6 p.m. ET tip in Detroit. He entered Sunday listed as questionable. It's not clear if the injury will sideline Dončić for multiple games.

Sunday's game against the Pistons was the first of a back-to-back. The Lakers will visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday.

A six-time All-NBA selection, Dončić is off to a sensational start to the season. Through nine games, Dončić is the NBA's leading scorer with averages of 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game while shooting 49.8% from the field and 41.9% on 13.8 3-point attempts per game.

The Lakers are off to their 9-2 start with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler anchoring the lineup in the first season since the departure of LeBron James. Dončić is playing like an MVP candidate as the primary driver behind the Lakers' strong start. The Lakers are certainly hoping that his back injury isn't one that will linger.

articles.title: Ultra-Rare Kobe Bryant Signed Lakers Jersey with NBA Finals Patch Sells for $1.8M at Auction
articles.summary: A Kobe Bryant jersey from the Los Angeles Lakers' run to the 2003-04 NBA Finals sold for $1.8 million at an auction from The Realest on Sunday.
articles.body:
A Kobe Bryant jersey from the Los Angeles Lakers' run to the 2003-04 NBA Finals sold for $1.8 million at an auction from The Realest on Sunday.

According to the site, Bryant wore the jersey across 17 total games in the 2003-04 season and eight playoff games. The Lakers were 16-1 overall in those games and 8-0 in those postseason contests.

Per the site, "This is the first and only championship-era No. 8 [Bryant Lakers' jersey] ever offered, in the uniform Kobe made famous, and no Kobe Bryant jersey of either number documented to double-digit games has a better record. It is also the only Kobe Bryant No. 8 jersey with an NBA Finals patch ever to come to market. It comes from the 2003-04 season Bryant would later identify as the origin of the Black Mamba persona, before the name became public mythology."

The Lakers reportedly sold the jersey after Bryant's retirement night in 2017, and before Sunday, it only ever had one owner. Somebody certainly paid a premium to become owner No. 2.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors Update Kevin Porter Jr.'s Potential Landing Spots After Bucks Exit
articles.summary: Kevin Porter Jr. has yet to find his new team after being waived by the Milwaukee Bucks in October, but that could change soon.
articles.body:
Kevin Porter Jr. has yet to find his new team after being waived by the Milwaukee Bucks in October, but that could change soon.

According to NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer , the veteran guard has drawn interest from the Sacramento Kings as they eye a replacement for Ben Simmons, who suffered a torn Achilles before the season started.

Stein and Fischer also noted that the Kings have shown interest in Gabe Vincent, who went unsigned as a free agent this offseason.

Stein and Fischer added that the Portland Trail Blazers and Miami Heat could be options for Porter if Sacramento chooses to sign Vincent.

Porter put up some of the best numbers of his career last year, averaging 17.4 points, 7.4 assists and 5.2 rebounds, though he played just 38 contests. Vincent, meanwhile, put up just 4.4 points per game across 53 games with the Los Angeles Lakers and Atlanta Hawks.

Signing with the Kings would be committing to the rebuild, since Sacramento is 1-8 so far and likely playing for the future. The Blazers are 6-3 to start the season, though Porter would likely have to come off the bench behind Damian Lillard or Ja Morant.

The Heat figure to be contenders with Giannis Antetokounmpo leading the way, though a 3-6 start suggests Miami still needs some help. Through the early going, it's clear the Heat need another piece in the backcourt.

articles.title: New Lakers Trade Rumors Reveal Nique Clifford Was Eyed by LA, More Before Thunder-Kings Deal
articles.summary: Nique Clifford is on his way to the Oklahoma City Thunder after being traded by the rebuilding Sacramento Kings on Sunday, but there reportedly were a handful of teams interested in him before the deal.
articles.body:
Nique Clifford is on his way to the Oklahoma City Thunder after being traded by the rebuilding Sacramento Kings on Sunday, but there reportedly were a handful of teams interested in him before the deal.

According to NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer , the Los Angeles Lakers, Denver Nuggets and Indiana Pacers were all interested in Clifford before he was dealt to the Thunder.

The Thunder traded a pair of second-round picks for Clifford, the 24th overall pick in the 2025 NBA draft. It's unclear what the other three teams were willing to give up for Clifford, but the Thunder ultimately won the race for the role player.

Clifford had a solid rookie season last year, averaging 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds and 2.4 assists off the bench. He played a small role so far this year, averaging just 6.3 minutes in Sacramento, but he should get some more playing time in OKC.

The Thunder have been rattled by injuries so far this season, with Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace both out for several months and potentially the rest of the season.

Clifford won't make up for their absences, but he'll at least give them some depth on the wing.

articles.title: Detroit Pistons Can Supercharge Their NBA Title Window with This Blockbuster Trade
articles.summary: Despite Jalen Duren being sidelined for most of the season so far, the Detroit Pistons continue to hover around the tippy top of the Eastern Conference. When you also consider the time Isaiah Joe has missed, the integration of John Collins and Ausar Thompson's revamped offensive role, this is a genuinely big deal.
articles.body:
Despite Jalen Duren being sidelined for most of the season so far, the Detroit Pistons continue to hover around the tippy top of the Eastern Conference. When you also consider the time Isaiah Joe has missed, the integration of John Collins and Ausar Thompson's revamped offensive role, this is a genuinely big deal.

Want to know what would be an even bigger deal?

Adding Naz Reid to the core and playoff-proofing the Pistons' offense once and for all.

Charlotte Hornets Receive: Ron Holland II, Detroit's 2027 first-round pick (unprotected), Detroit's 2029 first-round pick (top-four protection), $23.3 million trade exception (Naz Reid)

Chicago Bulls Receive: Kevin Huerter* (into room exception), 2029 second-round pick (most favorable of DET, MIL and NYK, via DET), Detroit's 2030 second-round pick, $3 million cash (via Charlotte)

*Note: This trade cannot be completed until Dec. 15.

Out: Ron Holland II, 2027 first-round pick, 2029 first-round pick, 2029 second-round pick, 2030 second-round pick

Detroit doesn't have to wait on a larger sample with Cade Cunningham, Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson to know it needs another long-term forward. John Collins is an imperfect, temporary answer.

Reid is a more permanent solution. He is in the heart of his prime at 27 years old. His contract has him under team control through 2028-29 at less than 15 percent of the salary cap. (He holds a 2029-30 player option.)

The offensive fit should be divine and effortless. Reid is shooting over 38 percent from deep on real volume over the past four years. While he doesn't need to dominate the ball, he has the reps as a creator to slide neatly into the second or third scorer's role, depending on where Duren settles.

Offloading Holland on top of two firsts can't be a deal-breaker just because he was a top-five pick in 2024. He looks more comfortable firing away from three this year, but defenses are never going to care. Javonte Green has also usurped him in the rotation. The Pistons already don't like to play him with Thompson.

The path to Holland panning out in Detroit is difficult to envision. The Pistons have already hurt his value by holding onto him this long. It's time for both parties to move on. It shouldn't be an especially hard call when at least one of the two first-rounders Detroit is surrendering will land in the 20s.

In: Ron Holland II, Detroit's 2027 first-round pick, Detroit's 2029 first-round pick, $23.3 million trade exception (Naz Reid)

Nothing suggests Charlotte has made Reid available after head coach Charles Lee benched him for the second half of the team's Oct. 28 game against, ironically, Detroit. But the Hornets' season is threatening to go off the rails.

Kon Knueppel hasn't been healthy all year. Brandon Miller is all over the place. Coby White began the season injured and is only a few games into his return. The offense desperately misses LaMelo Ball's shot-making and passing. (Who knew?!)

Charlotte didn't trade its only star with the intention of getting immediately better. That's sort of the point. The front office is clearly open to bigger-picture swings.

Acquiring Holland qualifies. His shooting limitations shouldn't be as much of an issue for the Hornets, who have plenty of spacers (in theory) but not enough playmaking avenues. His activity in transition, driving flashes and defensive hustle make him an intriguing running mate for a healthy Miller, Knueppel and White. With another year left on his rookie-scale deal, Charlotte has plenty of time to assess his fit.

Grabbing a 2027 first leaves the Hornets with up to four selections this June. That's trade-up ammo, baby. Or consolidation-trade goodies, friends. Detroit's 2029 first has some upside, knowing how quickly NBA windows open and shut these days.

Taking Holland's salary into the Ball trade exception also allows the Hornets to create another one for Reid. At the end of it all, they'd be left with two gargantuan TPEs: $23.3 million for Reid and $31.7 million remaining from LaMelo.

For what it's worth, the Hornets can take on Kevin Huerter if they want those seconds. But they'd have to waive a player first. Sending Huerter elsewhere lets them shave a total of $13.5 million off next year's payroll by going from Reid's $25 million to Holland's $11.5 million.

In: Kevin Huerter, 2029 second-round pick, 2030 second-round pick, $3 million cash

Reacquiring Huerter after shipping him to Detroit at last season's trade deadline is bound to get the Bulls meme'd. But this is a nice bit of business overall.

Executives around the league expect to receive one second-round pick for every $5 million in salary their squad gobbles up, per The Stein Line's Jake Fischer . Chicago is getting two seconds and $3 million in cash—the rough equivalent of $13 million.

Huerter is owed about $18 million between this season and next, with a team option for 2028-29. This puts the Bulls at a $5 million valuation deficit, which is more than reasonable when they're not taking on dead money.

Although Huerter's stroke has come-and-mostly-gone over the past few years, he's clearing 37 percent from distance this season. Defenses also respect his range and movement even when shots aren't falling.

Adding him helps what is the league's worst team from beyond the arc. With only one guaranteed year left on his contract after this one, the Bryson Graham-led front office might be able to parlay him into more second-round equity down the line.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: Dani Miret confirma la salida de Eli Ndiaye al Real Madrid: "Será su último partido"
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, acuciados por las lesiones en varias posiciones, recuperarán al jugador cedido
articles.summary: Los blancos, acuciados por las lesiones en varias posiciones, recuperarán al jugador cedido
articles.body: el Real Madrid vive momentos tortuosos con las lesiones. De repente se ha declarado en su vestuario una plaga de bajas que pasan por casi todos los puestos de la plantilla: Campazzo, Maledon, Jantunen, Deck, la de la temporada pasado de Garuba..., y al última de Chuma Okeke que se perdió el partido ante el UCAM Murcia. Tanta baja y sobre todo en el puesto específico de '4', hizo que el Madrid activara la opción de recuperar a Eli Ndiaye, cedido por los blancos al Asisa Joventut. Pedro Martínez ya dejó caer hace unos días que la opción era muy real. El problema es que los blancos tenían hasta el 15 de noviembre como fecha límite para ejecutarla. Dani Miret, entrenador de la Penya, confirmó tras su partido en Tenerife ante La Laguna, que Ndiaye se marchará rumbo al Madrid un día antes de que se cumpla ese 'deadline'. En una entrevista con Badalona Comunicació justo después del choque en Tenerife, Miret lo dejó claro: "Eli está completamente comprometido con la Penya y tiene muchísimas ganas de ayudarnos en este último partido", se refería Miret al choque ante el Casademont Zaragoza. "Después se marchará al Real Madrid, evidentemente, porque es lo que corresponde y porque su contrato está establecido de esa manera". El Joventut recibe al Casademont Zaragoza este próximo sábado a partir de las 21.00 horas. En la entrevista con Badalona Comunicació, Miret explica la operación con el Madrid: "Quiero explicar una cosa sobre Eli Ndiaye. Es un jugador que está totalmente comprometido con nosotros y que quiere estar aquí. La situación con el Real Madrid ha sido positiva para ambas partes. En su momento hicimos una buena operación porque conseguimos incorporar rápidamente a un jugador como Eli y reforzar el equipo. Pero que nadie piense que este jugador no tiene el compromiso de terminar haciendo un buen trabajo con nosotros y de cerrar su etapa en la Penya de la mejor manera posible". Falta que el Madrid lo anuncie de forma oficial, pero Eli Ndiaye jugará su último partido con el Joventut este sábado y al día siguiente ya se incorporará a la disciplina del Real Madrid que, dado las bajas en el equipo, necesita el concurso del hispanosenegalés.

articles.title: Giannis Reacts to Doc Rivers' Controversial Diss on Video After Reporter Told Him About the Comments
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo was "speechless" when it came to Doc Rivers' reflections of their time together on the Milwaukee Bucks.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo was "speechless" when it came to Doc Rivers' reflections of their time together on the Milwaukee Bucks.

"Oh, my God. First of all, he's not my coach. My coach is Coach Spo. But he's a guy, a coach that I've worked (with) in the past. I'm speechless. He made those comments today?," Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic's Eric Nehm .

"You have his number, right? You do. I know you do. You gotta go ask him why he thought that; that's on him. That's not on me. I gotta focus on my team and what I gotta do and how can I be better and how can I help the team.

"But like, goddamn. That's crazy. Never let bitterness and pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams, man. For every athlete out there, never let that (happen). That's insane, but you gotta go ask him why he said what he said. Not me."

Appearing on the Bill Simmons Podcast (via ESPN.com ), Rivers offered his candid opinion of Giannis' game. In general, he didn't believe there was a lot of subtlety or nuance to the two-time MVP's style.

"He's interesting. He's not easy," Rivers said. "He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy. ... He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

It's clear Antetokounmpo took exception to those remarks.

Attacking the basket has always been a big facet of Giannis' offensive approach. Somebody with his size (6'11"), strength and agility would've been foolish not to play downhill toward the rim.

Something worth considering is how much Rivers' perspective is influenced by coaching Milwaukee at a time when the franchise's championship window was closing.

Midway through the 2023-24 season, it was clear the Bucks were hitting a wall. Acquiring Damian Lillard ahead of that year was a sign of the organization's urgency.

As Milwaukee's performance steadily declined, Antetokounmpo may have felt he had to do even more on his own. Things weren't clicking with Lillard, and Khris Middleton was no longer the effective scorer he had been.

Giannis' trademark drives into the paint were one way to create instant offense.

Was that sustainable? Obviously not, based on the the Bucks losing in the first round of the 2024 and 2025 playoffs before missing the postseason entirely in 2025-26.

Having Antetokounmpo play more within the flow of the offense probably wouldn't have changed anything, though.

Rivers joined a sinking ship in January 2024, and that was a recipe to create a tenure nobody would remember all that fondly.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Relationship 'Cratered' Due to 'Outside Influences,' New NBA Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The relationship between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum on the Boston Celtics may have suffered under the weight of nine years' worth of rumors and speculation over their fit together.
articles.body:
The relationship between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum on the Boston Celtics may have suffered under the weight of nine years' worth of rumors and speculation over their fit together.

The Athletic's Jay King laid out the factors leading to Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers and the supposed bad blood between he and Tatum.

Rather than one inciting incident that pitted the two against one another, King described the dynamic as "a productive working partnership that endured a long list of ups and downs before eventually cratering under the weight of outside influences."

One source flatly told King that "there was no conflict," and Celtics guard Derrick White echoed the sentiment.

"I didn't feel any (tension)," he said. "Those are two guys that wanted to win. Two guys that are really talented that can do a lot of different things and competed at that level together. I didn't think there were any problems. No beef."

This was the general narrative that got presented in the immediate aftermath of Brown's trade. In recent weeks, fans started to wonder whether there was more to the story.

Brown used the cap emoji when commenting on a video of Tatum recounting his surprise to learn the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was on his way out:

Brown raised some eyebrows again when he told reporters he has "no beef" with Tatum but asserted the six-time All-Star has a "hell of a PR team."

Ultimately, the situation might be as straightforward as it looks.

When Boston couldn't get over the hump, a lot of people wondered whether the team had hit its ceiling with the tandem of Brown and Tatum. The former was regularly floated in blockbuster trades intended to deliver a championship.

Finally winning a title only brought a brief respite.

Eventually, the conversation shifted to whether the Celtics could afford to pay both of their big stars and still contend. Tatum's Achilles injury presented an unexpected variable as Brown thrived with the spotlight to himself. It was a role he wouldn't maintain once Tatum was healthy.

After nearly a decade of hearing the same broad speculation, a breakup in some form was probably needed, and the Celtics clearly picked Tatum as the cornerstone they'd continue to build around.

articles.title: LeBron James responds after man arrested for stalking at 76ers star's house in Los Angeles: 'My family is safe'
articles.summary: A man was arrested Friday for wandering onto LeBron James' property.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James said he was still "looking into everything" after a man was arrested at James' Los Angeles property on Friday.

Speaking with reporters Sunday, James said his family was safe and called that " the most important " thing. He did not go into too much detail on the situation otherwise.

Reports emerged Friday that a man was arrested for felony stalking after appearing at James' home in Brentwood, California. The LAPD was initially called out to investigate a report of a possible burglary at the residence, according to ESPN.

Officers found a man on the property and arrested him for stalking , per ABCNews. The arrest was made without incident and no one was at James' home at the time of the arrest. The man reportedly did not go inside the house and was not armed, per police.

Felony stalking can result in up to three years in state prison , a fine of up to $10,000 or both in California, according to Kann California Law Group.

At the time of the incident, James was on a road trip with the 76ers. He returned to his old home, Cleveland, Friday evening, where he took on the Cavaliers. On Sunday, James and the 76ers played the Chicago Bulls in Chicago.

If James was unnerved by the arrest, it didn't show in his play Sunday. James dropped 22 points during the team's 127-122 win over the Bulls.

articles.title: Lakers' New Ideal NBA Trade Targets Following Anthony Davis Rumors and Speculation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers currently sit in first place in the Western Conference but could still use a piece or two as they chase their first NBA title since 2020.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers currently sit in first place in the Western Conference but could still use a piece or two as they chase their first NBA title since 2020.

Do not expect one of those pieces to be a member of that last championship squad.

ESPN NBA insider Brian Windhorst refuted speculation that the team could reunite with Anthony Davis during an appearance on the Sedano and Kap Morning Show. He noted that Davis has a player option for the 2027-28 season and the Wizards want to see him play 20-30 games before deciding what they will do with him.

Davis would be a risky addition anyway, with his recent injury history and unproven chemistry with franchise star Luka Dončić.

There are better options for the Lakers, who can both help compliment the team's superstar and provide an upgrade at positions of need.

Look no further than the New Orleans Pelicans, where Herb Jones or Trey Murphy would provide defensive and wing help, two areas that the Lakers absolutely must upgrade if they hope to compete for a title.

Insider Jake Fisher reported during an appearance on SiriusXM NBA Radio that the team would be interested in acquiring Jericho Sims from the Milwaukee Bucks.

Sims is a low-cost center with great athleticism, who could provide depth behind Walker Kessler at a key position. He has not been utilized to his fullest potential this season and a fresh start, for a team who could benefit from his abilities, would be best for him.

Considering the Lakers are already over the cap, and do not have a wealth of protected draft picks to send in return for a higher-profile player, finding low-cost hidden gems like Sims who can fill areas of need is in the best interest of the organization and its front office now and leading up to the trade deadline.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo says he's 'speechless' over criticism from former coach Doc Rivers: 'That's insane'
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo eventually mentioned "bitterness and pettiness" when discussing Doc Rivers' comments.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo was "speechless" over criticism from his former Milwaukee Bucks coach Doc Rivers.

Rivers made those comments during an appearance on "The Bill Simmons Podcast," which was posted Thursday. During the episode, Rivers said Antetokounmpo wanted to leave the Bucks but wouldn't ask for a trade so he could continue being viewed as the good guy.

Rivers later added that Antetokounmpo "doesn't necessarily have this super IQ" and that he "really has one way: Downhill, force, force."

When asked about those comments Sunday, Antetokounmpo initially said he was "speechless" before trying to brush them aside , per ESPN.

"First of all, he's not my coach," Antetokounmpo told reporters after Miami's 114-108 victory over the Sacramento Kings. "My coach is Coach Spo [Erik Spoelstra], but [Rivers] is a guy — a coach — that I've worked with in the past. I'm speechless." "You got to go ask him why he thought that," Antetokounmpo said. "That's on him, that's not on me. I just got to focus on my team and what I got to do and how I can be better and how can I help the team."

"First of all, he's not my coach," Antetokounmpo told reporters after Miami's 114-108 victory over the Sacramento Kings. "My coach is Coach Spo [Erik Spoelstra], but [Rivers] is a guy — a coach — that I've worked with in the past. I'm speechless."

"You got to go ask him why he thought that," Antetokounmpo said. "That's on him, that's not on me. I just got to focus on my team and what I got to do and how I can be better and how can I help the team."

Later on, however, Antetokounmpo implied Rivers was fueled by "bitterness and pettiness."

"But God, that's crazy. Never let bitterness or pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams. For every athlete out there, never let that — that's insane. But you got to go ask him why he said what he said. Not me."

Heat coach Erik Spoelstra was also asked about Rivers' comments. The Heat coach declined to feed into them, saying he liked and respected Rivers.

Rivers and Antetokounmpo worked together for two-and-a-half years in Milwaukee. While the team made the playoffs in two of those seasons, it disappointed, falling in the first round in both years.

Antetokounmpo performed extremely well in his first two years under Rivers, averaging 30.4 points per game. The star big man spent a large stretch of last season injured.

The Bucks responded to the down year by jettisoning both men. Rivers stepped down from his role as head coach and Antetokounmpo was traded to the Heat. Rivers opted to return to the broadcast booth for the 2026-27 NBA season. Antetokounmpo is averaging 27.5 points and 12.8 rebounds in his first season with the Heat.

articles.title: Women's basketball AP Poll: South Carolina holds No. 1 spot after dominant early wins as Michigan, Oklahoma climb

The Gamecocks remained at No. 1 in the first true Associated Press poll of the season on Monday, thanks to an opening win against Maryland and then a 45-point blowout over North Carolina to open the new season.

South Carolina held on late to beat Maryland in its opener in Paris, and then returned to the United States for a dominant outing against the Tar Heels. Chloe Kitts had a double-double in that second contest, which was essentially over at halftime.

UConn bounced back after that, however, and beat Iowa behind a 39-point outing from Sarah Strong on Sunday. The Hawkeyes remained at No. 10, and share that spot with UConn this week.

USC, now with JuJu Watkins back, remained at No. 3 in the poll. Duke rounded out the top five.

The Huskies have a big week ahead of them, with a matchup against No. 17 Ohio State on Thursday and then against No. 7 Louisville on Sunday.
