articles.title: Carmelo Anthony Details Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum's 'Final' Interaction Before Celtics-76ers Trade
articles.summary: In late June, before Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, both he and Jayson Tatum attended the Cannes Sports Beach Event after-party.
articles.body:
In late June, before Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, both he and Jayson Tatum attended the Cannes Sports Beach Event after-party.

But according to Gary Washburn of the Boston Globe , Brown—who was on the trade block at the time—reportedly asked to be seated at a VIP table with Carmelo Anthony after being informed that Tatum was also at the event.

"I thought [Brown] felt awkward about something going on," Anthony said. "He didn't know what was going on at the time. I know JT was on the other side. I know Jaylen [wanted to speak with Jayson] but he didn't know what to do. I just told him, 'Why don't you just go over there to JT?' "He was like, 'Man, I don't know where we are at. Do you mind if I just stay here?' I was like, 'Of course.'"

The disconnect between Brown and Tatum has continued since the trade. Tatum has insisted that he was in the dark regarding the deal. Brown pushed back on that assertion, eventually saying that Tatum has a "great PR team" and noting that there's "no beef" between the pair but there "might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. He should stay ready at all times."

Washburn reported that the Celtics treated Tatum like the definitive franchise cornerstone and it caused some tension between Brown and the organization, even after it was Brown who was the Eastern Conference Finals and NBA Finals MVP during the team's 2023-24 championship season. The team took longer to negotiate a max contract with Brown when he was eligible for one than they did with Tatum. The organization didn't love the profile of his on-court analytics and felt that there was an "increasing lack of on-court chemistry" between Brown and Tatum, that the duo had become "a relic."

Brown's case for earning a bit more respect throughout the years was only bolstered when he led the Celtics to a 56-26 record last season while Tatum recovered from a torn Achilles and had a career year (28.7 PPG, 6.9 RPG, 5.1 APG).

But even if the Celtics had internally decided they wanted to focus building the team around Tatum, the starring duo likely could have pushed to stay together.

As Washburn wrote, "Ideally, the superstars could have discussed their future together in Boston and perhaps made a pact to take less money so the team could afford a stronger supporting cast. That discussion never happened. According to multiple sources, Brown and Tatum were asked to talk about their roles and partnership before Tatum returned from his Achilles injury in March. They were left alone in a room to talk, but it remains unclear what was said and whether it had any impact on their relationship."

And that is perhaps where Brown doesn't fully buy Tatum's assertion that he was in the dark about the eventual trade. While Washburn noted that the "Celtics' front office did not keep Tatum informed on the Brown trade talks" and that it's the organization's "philosophy that star players should not be involved in personnel decisions involving teammates," plenty of rumors about Brown being on the trade block were swirling about. If Tatum pushed hard to keep Brown in Boston it would have carried at least some weight.

But as Washburn wrote, "The fact Tatum stayed out of it appeared to make Brown more isolated."

It's all a moot point now. Brown's Sixers are 9-2 and he's quickly carved out a role for himself as a secondary scorer behind Tyrese Maxey and a defensive presence on the wing. The Celtics are right behind them in the standings at 8-2, with Paul George playing a complementary role behind Tatum.

But when the two teams meet for the first time in the regular season on Tuesday night in Philadelphia, there will be a charge in the air. The animosity between the longtime rivals was already high, especially after the Sixers eliminated the Celtics in the first round of the playoffs last season, and the subplot between Brown and Tatum has undoubtedly raised the stakes.

articles.title: AP College Basketball Poll 2026 Released for First Regular-Season Men's Rankings
articles.summary: UCLA jumped 13 spots after opening the 2026-27 men's college basketball season with an upset of Arizona.
articles.body:
UCLA jumped 13 spots after opening the 2026-27 men's college basketball season with an upset of Arizona.

The Bruins are ninth in the new Associated Press Top 25 poll . The Wildcats, who had been fifth, are now down in 12th.

Florida consolidated its position atop the rankings with a 77-67 win over Miami and collected 53 first-place votes, while UConn made a statement by taking down reigning national champion 85-77.

Virginia is knocking on the door of the top five thanks to a 91-72 blowout of Arkansas

All things considered, an eight-point loss to the Huskies wasn't a bad showing from the Wolverines given how much change they underwent in the offseason. UConn did, however, lead by as many as 18 points and was in control for almost the entire contest.

"As I've said for two months now, this team isn't defending a national championship," Michigan coach Mike Boynton said . "They're trying to establish their own legacy. I think today was a great step forward."

The Wolverines only have one more ranked non-conference opponent (No. 11 Louisville on Dec. 5). That gives them a lot of opportunities to build some continuity between all of the new additions and few holdovers from the 2025-26 squad.

Continuity appears to be a strength for Florida.

Last year, the Gators opened with a loss to Arizona, which served as a preview of what was to come before they tipped off SEC play. Their collective strength was too much for Miami.

Thomas Haugh had a double-double (19 points and 10 rebounds) against the Hurricanes. Rueben Chinyelu collected 14 boards. And Alex Condon (11 points) and Boogie Fland (12 points) each scored in double figures. Florida also held Miami to 35 percent shooting overall and 4-of-17 on three-pointers.

UCLA coach Mick Cronin isn't on the hot seat after reaching the NCAA tournament in five of the past six years. Some other notable programs in Westwood are raising the bar, though.

The women's basketball team is the reigning national champion, while the football team is off to a 9-0 start and owns top-five status in the AP poll .

Toppling Arizona was a great way for the men's team to tip things off. Ivan Kharchenkov had a monster game (38 points and 10 rebounds) for the Wildcats, but it wasn't enough to overcome the Bruins' balance.

Looking ahead this week, college basketball fans will want to make sure their schedules are clear Tuesday night.

Michigan State and Duke head to Chicago for a 7 p.m. ET matchup, with Kansas vs. Kentucky to follow at United Center. At 8 p.m., Texas Tech will host Illinois at 8 p.m. for another Top 25 tilt.

articles.title: Why Celtics Felt Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum Were 'Incapable' of 2nd NBA Title Revealed in New Rumors
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star guard Jaylen Brown is facing his old franchise for the first time in Monday night's game against the Boston Celtics, and more details have emerged about the end of his tenure with the team.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star guard Jaylen Brown is facing his old franchise for the first time in Monday night's game against the Boston Celtics, and more details have emerged about the end of his tenure with the team.

Gary Washburn of The Boston Globe reported that part of the reason why the Celtics opted to trade Brown to the Sixers was that they didn't feel he and star forward Jayson Tatum would be able to win a second championship together.

"There was a belief inside the organization that the Celtics were incapable of winning another championship with the pairing," Washburn stated. "They were too similar and too predictable in the fourth quarter, when they would take turns trying to score against ramped-up defenses while their teammates watched. Their lack of success in the New York series in 2025 and the devastating Philadelphia series loss in the first round in May cemented the organization's thinking."

Brown and Tatum helped lead the Celtics to the 2024 NBA championship, with Brown taking home Finals MVP honors. Boston failed to advance past the second round of the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, creating questions about the duo's effectiveness.

According to Washburn, "The increasing lack of on-court chemistry and Brown's disappointing analytical numbers contributed to the Celtics pursuing the controversial trade. Sources say the front office felt the two-headed wing arsenal of Tatum and Brown had simply become a relic."

After going their separate ways, it doesn't appear that Brown and Tatum are missing their former partnership. Brown's Sixers lead the Atlantic Division with a 9-2 record, and he's been thriving while playing in a star-studded lineup that also includes LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. Tatum has led the Celtics to an 8-2 record while serving as the team's No.1 option.

Brown indicated there was no love lost between him and his former teammate when he told reporters that he had no plans to speak to Tatum ahead of Monday's game.

"It's nothing to talk about. I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said after scoring 29 points in Sunday's 127-121 win over the Chicago Bulls. "Just playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win, so it's nothing to talk about. Just check the ball up."

Still, fans will be watching closely to see how Brown and Tatum interact with one another in their first meeting as opponents.

articles.title: Men's basketball AP poll: Florida solidifies No. 1 ranking as Arizona, Michigan tumble
articles.summary: The top four teams in the poll each picked up back-to-back wins to open the new season.
articles.body:
We're a week into the college basketball season, and Florida is still on top.

The Gators, after a solid 10-point win over Miami on opening night , held onto their No. 1 ranking Monday in the first true Associated Press poll of the season.

They looked every bit like the favorite to win the national championship that came with their preseason ranking last month on both sides of the ball, too. Thomas Haugh, who opted to remain at Florida despite the fact that he would have been a first-round NBA Draft pick, led the way with 19 points and 10 rebounds. They shut the Hurricanes down in the second half, too. As a result of the loss, Miami fell three spots to No. 17 in this week's poll.

The top four teams in the poll remained unchanged, too, after all started out the season with a pair of wins. Duke remained at No. 2 after a pair of easy wins, though the Blue Devils have No. 5 Michigan State waiting for them on Tuesday night. Illinois won its first two games by an average of 58.5 points to retain the third spot. The Illini will have their first true test of the season against No. 16 Texas Tech in Lubbock on Tuesday, too.

And UConn remained at No. 4 after back-to-back wins , including one over the defending champions in Boston. The Huskies took advantage of a very different Michigan team than the one that beat them in the title game in April, and Braylon Mullins dropped 23 points. As a result, Michigan fell to No. 20.

The first major movement in the poll came from Arizona, which fell to UCLA on the first night of the season. The Bruins led nearly the entire way in that contest, and even jumped up by 16 at halftime. They moved up 13 spots to No. 9 in this week's poll, while Arizona slid down to No. 12. The Wildcats did bounce back with a 20-point blowout over Cal Poly days later, and Ivan Kharchenkov put up 38 points in the loss to UCLA. Arizona, even with the early loss, looks to be a true threat in the Big 12.

As for Florida, things won't get much easier. The Gators have Florida State up next on Tuesday night, and then have matchups with Notre Dame and Duke before SEC play really gets going. But for now, the season got off exactly the way they expected it to in Gainesville.

articles.summary: Maxima Roma, Valencia, Dubai, Hapoel Tel Aviv, PAOK y Paris pasarán a ser también dueños del torneo. Wildcards de tres años para Estrella Roja, Partizan, Napoles y Virtus Bolonia
articles.body: La Euroliga acaba de dar un paso decisivo en su consolidación como la gran competición de clubes del baloncesto europeo con la elección de seis nuevas franquicias que se incorporarán a su proyecto: Maxima Roma, Valencia Basket, Dubai Basketball, Hapoel Tel Aviv, PAOK Salónica y Paris Basketball, según adelanta La Gazzeta Dello Sport y ha podido confirmar MARCA con algunos de los rectores de la competición. Siguiendo la directiva que los propietarios hicieron en su última Asamblea General celebrada en Como para la conversión de los grandes candidatos en franquicias para proseguir así con la expansión y tras estudiar las recomendaciones del Board sobre la primera lista confeccionada, la Euroliga ha decidido que sean esas seis ciudades con sus equipos las nuevas integrantes del torneo, a falta de la aprobación de la conversión y expansión que tendrá lugar en la asamblea que se celebrará a finales de este mes de noviembre. Esta selección estratégica permitirá a la Euroliga ampliar la competición de 20 a 24 equipos a partir de la temporada 2027-28 (los clubes propietarios, más los seis nuevos, más cuatro wildcards, más dos plazas para la Eurocup) con el objetivo de alcanzar los 28 en 2030. Con esta operación, no solo amplía su número de participantes, sino que refuerza su posición como referencia del baloncesto de clubes en Europa y blinda buena parte de su futuro estratégico. El modelo elegido también representa un cambio estructural: las nuevas entidades accederán al estatus de franquicia mediante cuotas de entrada que oscilarán entre los 50 y los 90 millones de euros, integrándose en un proyecto que aspira a dotar de estabilidad y continuidad a sus participantes. Más allá de la incorporación de nuevos clubes, la decisión supone una apuesta por mercados y ciudades de enorme valor deportivo, económico y estratégico. Roma, Valencia, París, Dubái, Tel Aviv y Salónica aportan nuevos focos de interés, amplían la dimensión geográfica de la Euroliga y refuerzan su capacidad para atraer aficionados, patrocinadores e inversores. La combinación de grandes capitales, mercados emergentes y ciudades con tradición baloncestística configura una red de franquicias que hace mucho más difícil que cualquier proyecto alternativo pueda disputarle su espacio y su influencia en el continente. La expansión contempla, además, cuatro licencias temporales de tres años para dos clubes serbios, Partizan y Estrella Roja, y otros dos equipos italianos, Virtus Bolonia y Napoles, con prioridad para futuras plazas permanentes al atravesar en la actualidad por coyunturas complicadas de diversa índole que dificultan su planificación presente para incorporarse ya como franquicias. Los dos equipos serbios, con el cambio de gobierno en su país, están sujetos a cierta inestabilidad para su financiación. El Nápoles, volcado en su nuevo pabellón de 250 millones prefiere esperar dos o tres años, y la Virtus Bolonia, con el cambio de propietario, necesita primero estabilizar su situación financiera. Pero son cuatro equipos muy queridos por la Euroliga, que les tendrá muy cerca y en la lista de espera para incorporarlos de manera definitiva en cuanto sus situaciones particulares se consoliden. El movimiento adquiere especial relevancia ante los planes de la NBA de desarrollar una competición propia en Europa. La Euroliga se adelanta, define sus territorios, incorpora nuevos socios y consolida su estructura con independencia del desenlace de las negociaciones con la liga estadounidense. El mensaje es claro: se postula para liderar el futuro del baloncesto europeo y está dando pasos de gigante para hacerlo. Tras ver rechazada su oferta inicial, la NBA anunció que tendría tiempo para negociar hasta que la transformación de los clubes en franquicias se hiciera efectiva, por lo que la reunión de la Junta Directiva de la Euroliga a finales de mes, en la que se aprobará la expansión con las seis nuevas franquicias, representa otra encrucijada en el asunto, quizás la definitiva.

articles.title: 2028 NBA All-Star Location Reportedly Being Finalized for Host's 1st Time in 38 Years
articles.summary: The NBA is taking the 2028 All-Star Game to South Florida.
articles.body:
The NBA is taking the 2028 All-Star Game to South Florida.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Kaseya Center in Miami will host the midseason spectacle, its first time staging the event since 1990.

Given both the weather and nightlife scene in the city, some might be surprised to learn Miami hasn't been a regular in the All-Star Game rotation. Heat president of business operations Eric Woolworth has floated the idea for a decade.

The Miami Herald 's Anthony Chiang presented the context behind the situation:

"Previous NBA All-Star Games were usually held on Presidents' Day Weekend in February, which is the same weekend that the Miami International Boat Show is held. That conflict led to the long hiatus, with the boat show using the Miami Beach Convention Center and taking up a large chunk of hotel rooms in the area."

According to Chiang, the 2028 Miami International Boat Show is getting moved out of its usual slot on the calendar. As a result, the city became a realistic possibility for the All-Star Game.

Chiang also reported the NBA brought the idea to Heat officials rather than the other way around.

Miami will be another warmer-weather climate for the All-Star Game after a stretch of the festivities heading to more frigid cities. Across a five-year period, All-Star Weekend went to Chicago, Cleveland, Salt Lake City and Indianapolis.

"If I could change something about All-Star Weekends, they wouldn't be in cold-weather cities anymore," nine-time All-Star Paul George jokingly said to reporters in 2024.

He got his wish as the event went to San Francisco in 2025 and Inglewood, California, the following year. Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix will be the site for the 2027 installment.

articles.title: Miami reportedly to host NBA All-Star Game in 2028 for first time since 1990
articles.summary: Somehow, the NBA's February All-Star break has taken place in Miami only once.
articles.body:
The NBA All-Star Game is returning to Miami.

Per ESPN's Shams Charania , the NBA is finalizing Miami as the host city of the league's 2028 All-Star Weekend.

Despite being a prime destination for a February party, this will mark just the second time that Miami has hosted the NBA's All-Star weekend. The first and only other time was in 1990, the second season of the Heat's existence.

Magic Johnson won MVP in that game , while David Robinson, Reggie Miller, Dennis Rodman and Scottie Pippen all made their All-Star debuts.

Since Miami last hosted, 10 NBA cities have hosted multiple All-Star weekends : Los Angeles (4 times), New Orleans (3 times), Atlanta, Charlotte, Cleveland, Houston, New York, Orlando, Phoenix and Salt Lake City (2 times each). The Bay Area has also hosted twice since 1990 with games in Oakland and in San Francisco.

Phoenix will host again in February from the 19-21.

As currently iterated, the NBA All-Star weekend officially consists of the Rising Stars Game on Friday night, the skills contest, 3-point contest and dunk contest on All-Star Saturday and the All-Star Game itself on Sunday.

articles.title: Viral Video of Bronny James, NBA Fan Addressed by Pistons Spokesperson Following Lakers Game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James was seen in a viral video confronting a heckler during Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James was seen in a viral video confronting a heckler during Sunday's game against the Detroit Pistons.

A Pistons spokesperson told The Athletic's Hunter Patterson that the fans "were removed from their seats for violating courtside conduct policy and offered seating in a different location away from the court."

James, who is in his third season with the Lakers, has played in five games this year in limited action. He was assigned to Los Angeles' G League affiliate on Thursday. He averaged 18.4 points on 49.6 percent shooting, 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 25 G League games over the past two seasons.

James has been no stranger to hecklers throughout his young career. As the son of legendary Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James, the 22-year-old has faced a high level of scrutiny since he entered the league.

In addition to James' confrontation with the fans on Sunday, Lakers star guard Austin Reaves was seen having an interaction with another courtside fan before halftime. Reaves got face-to-face with the fan before his teammates and the referees stepped in, and he waved in that fan's direction after hitting a game-sealing three-pointer to cap a 43-point performance in the Lakers' 121-116 win.

The Lakers lead the Western Conference with a 9-2 record and are riding a five-game win streak into Monday night's matchup against the Atlanta Hawks (7-4), so the team isn't looking for more drama going forward.

articles.title: 10 Hardest NBA Stars To Coach, Featuring Giannis Antetokounmpo
articles.summary: We rank the 10 hardest NBA stars to coach in the league right now, featuring the recently criticized Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
Coaching an NBA superstar is supposed to be a privilege, but it can get ugly at times. There isn't a better example than the criticism aimed at Miami Heat superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo courtesy of Doc Rivers .

Doc Rivers singled out Giannis Antetokounmpo as the most difficult superstar he has ever coached . On the Bill Simmons podcast :

"He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace," Rivers said. "He's really a difficult guy. I was telling someone this: he has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have super IQ at the same time. It's really a strange thing. And he really has one way. Downhill, force, like every play. He wants to force it.

"There's times where I wish he did one thing," Rivers continued. "I wish he learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys that you get a lot of them from the U.S., AAU guys that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team.

"And I told Giannis this: the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. "How important it is when you're in practice and shootarounds to lock in on execution. And now he has a coach who is as good as there is in execution."

Giannis did not exactly embrace the characterization, appearing defensive in his response and pushing back against the criticism in his postgame interview:

"Oh, my God," Antetokounmpo said, via Eric Nehm. "First of all, he's not my coach. My coach is Coach [Erik Spoelstra]. But he's a coach that I've worked in the past. I'm speechless. He made those comments when? Today?"

To be fair, there were some coming to his defense. Erik Spoelstra obviously defended his player , but so did Jason Kidd , who also coached the Greek Freak in the past.

The exchange begs the interesting question: Is Antetokounmpo really one of the NBA's most challenging players to coach, or is his demanding and competitive personality completely misunderstood?

Well, we think Giannis has to be one of the toughest superstars to coach, and here are 10 NBA stars who present some of the toughest coaching challenges in the league.

Rudy Gobert is one of the NBA's greatest defenders, but coaching him requires accepting some limitations. His rim protection, rebounding, and ability to erase mistakes make him incredibly valuable, but he is often offensively inept.

Gobert is not somebody you can simply throw into every lineup and expect the same results. His inability to consistently punish smaller defenders or create his own offense becomes problematic against teams that attack his weaknesses. Not an easy job for Chris Finch to figure things out on offense.

The real headache comes when the playoffs arrive, and opponents start pulling him away from the basket. Finch must decide whether Gobert's defensive brilliance outweighs the spacing problems and small-ball vulnerabilities he can introduce.

We have to make it clear: Gobert is absolutely worth coaching. But maximizing him requires considerably more creativity than his defensive reputation might suggest.

Kyrie Irving is incredibly gifted, and he can get the crowd going in an instant. The problem is that Irving has never been particularly interested in allowing basketball to completely dictate his personal life or individuality.

His career has featured several high-profile departures and complicated relationships with organizations, and it often feels like coaches are walking on needles with the future Hall of Famer. Rookie head coach Dusty May hasn't had issues with Kyrie so far, and his talented guard has held his own at times this season.

But still, coaching Irving needs a delicate balance between authority and trust. A traditional disciplinarian approach is unlikely to work particularly well with someone who is an independent thinker, while giving him too much freedom can create problems for the broader organization.

Irving's basketball talent is not the issue; getting everyone aligned around a common direction is the challenge. Irving can make a coach look brilliant or foolish at the same time, but we guess that just comes with being the GOAT of dribbling a basketball.

Zion Williamson is one of the most frustrating coaching challenges in the NBA because the talent is so extraordinary and the expectations are always so enormous. When healthy, Williamson is virtually unstoppable attacking the basket.

However, questions surrounding his conditioning, availability, and consistency have hindered his development. Coaches are not simply responsible for designing an offense around Zion; they also have to worry about keeping their franchise centerpiece physically ready. As if coaches don't have enough to worry about.

The pressure is particularly intense because the Pelicans have continued investing in Williamson as their future, even when the results have not consistently justified that faith. That puts enormous responsibility on Jamahl Mosley to push him, hold him accountable, and somehow maintain a relationship without losing the player emotionally.

There is no easy answer when your most talented player requires constant attention to physical preparation. It might have been easier back in the day to whip a player into shape, but player empowerment has made Zion a tough player to figure out.

Giannis Antetokounmpo is the most physically overwhelming superstar in basketball, but that dominance can be too much for coaches, hence what Doc Rivers spoke about. Giannis' instinct is to impose his physicality on opponents rather than patiently dissecting every defensive coverage.

That mentality is responsible for much of his greatness, but it can become problematic when opponents build defensive walls and force him into uncomfortable half-court situations. Perhaps that is why the Miami Heat have gotten off to a terrible 4-6 start so far.

Doc Rivers described Giannis as the most difficult superstar he has coached, and he has a point. The disagreement between Rivers and Giannis highlights an uncomfortable reality: coaching an incredibly competitive player sometimes means challenging the very instincts that made him a superstar.

Giannis wants to dominate, and slowing him down or asking him to change his approach is not necessarily going to be received well. We have seen it with players such as Russell Westbrook, and Giannis might fit that mold. His intensity is an enormous asset, but convincing him that the best basketball decision should be to slow down won't always work out.

Draymond Green is one of the best defensive players of his generation, and his basketball IQ makes him an extension of the coaching staff on the floor. Without Green, the Warriors would not have won four championships as the greatest modern dynasty. We recognize that.

Unfortunately, that same intensity can become a nightmare when emotions take over. Technical fouls, fights, ejections, and suspensions have placed Golden State in difficult situations, forcing Steve Kerr to have to deal with the cleanup afterwards.

The challenge is that Green cannot simply be coached like an ordinary role player. His voice carries enormous weight in the locker room, and his relationship with teammates, particularly Stephen Curry, is central to the Warriors' identity.

Kerr must know when to empower him, when to pull him back, and when to accept that his emotional volatility could cost the team. Add his limited scoring to the equation, and Green is a tough player to handle. Kudos to Kerr, who has done as much as anyone could have.

Kawhi Leonard is the ultimate coaching paradox: he is an elite two-way superstar who can change a team's championship goals, but his availability is one of the most difficult variables to manage. Think about this: coaches have to always worry about whether Kawhi plays or not, and the team has to constantly change because of that.

Then there is the communication challenge. Leonard is famously reserved and has gotten away with almost everything in his career so far. His personal approach to managing his career is highly independent, meaning coaches must often navigate a more discreet relationship rather than constant verbal engagement.

The frustration is obvious: when Kawhi is available, he can be one of the best players in the world. But building a championship system around an injury-prone and polarizing personality is a tough job for any coach. Hats off to Darko Rajakovic for keeping the Raptors competitive with Kawhi missing a few games already.

Joel Embiid is a nightmare matchup for opposing defenses, but coaching him could also be a nightmare at times. His injury history, conditioning concerns, and availability have forced coaching staffs to reconsider their plans. You best believe that Nick Nurse is constantly thinking about Embiid's minutes in every game this season.

When Embiid is healthy, Philadelphia can build an entire championship-caliber offense around his ability to score from anywhere. When he is unavailable, however, everything changes. And that's even the case for the current superteam 76ers.

There is also the tactical challenge of maximizing Embiid's offensive preferences. His ability to draw fouls and operate from the mid-range can be devastating, but it occasionally slows the offense and limits opportunities for teammates to attack in rhythm.

Embiid's emotional reactions, visible frustrations, and occasional disagreements with teammates or coaching decisions add another layer of complexity. He is a generational talent, but managing his physical condition and temperament is an enormous undertaking. Perhaps having LeBron James on the roster will signficantly help Nurse's incredibly tough job for this season.

Trae Young is an offensive system on his own, but coaching him means building an offense that moves around a very specific set of preferences. Young thrives with the ball in his hands, particularly in pick-and-roll situations where he can manipulate defenders.

The problem is that this approach can become predictable and overly dependent on one player. If there is a slight variety, Young's impact will significantly decline. That makes it a Trae-or-die system for a player on a max deal.

Defensively, the challenge is even more obvious. Young's physical limitations make him a player opponents actively target, forcing coaching staffs to develop schemes that protect him and prevent opposing guards from exploiting mismatches. Talk about headaches.

Trae can carry an offense, but building a contender around him needs a ton of patience, creativity, and a willingness to accommodate his strengths while confronting his weaknesses.

Luka Doncic is the frontrunner for MVP this season and the best basketball system in the NBA. Nobody can control an offense better right now, so that's a luxury JJ Redick has.

But coaching Luka requires accepting that the offense will frequently operate according to his rhythm, preferences, and decision-making. His heliocentric style can produce spectacular results, but it might come back to bite the Lakers in the playoffs. Redick is likely fully aware of that.

The psychological management is just as demanding, by the way. Luka's constant frustration with officials, frequent complaints, and emotional reactions to unfavorable calls can become distractions that opponents exploit.

Coaches have constantly encouraged him to maintain composure, and it just looks bad across the board at times. His talent is so overwhelming that challenging his habits becomes a delicate balancing act.

Luka can make virtually any coach look like a genius, but getting him to consistently embrace the less glamorous aspects of winning basketball is another matter entirely. Let's see how far Redick can go in that regard.

James Harden tops this list because coaching him has always involved making sure everything else is in order. Harden is one of the greatest offensive players of his generation, but he has to do it his way.

His step-back three-pointer and pick-and-roll mastery are legendary, but the same strengths can become limitations when a coach wants more variety in the offense. With Harden, the offense goes as Harden goes. It doesn't even matter that Donovan Mitchell is beside him right now.

His complicated history with many franchises makes the challenge even more compelling. Houston, Brooklyn, and Philadelphia all experienced turbulence surrounding his relationships with organizational leadership, and it seems that you can't make Harden happy.

Harden is not difficult to coach because of his amazing skill set; he is difficult because his preferences can become the foundation around which everything else must revolve. Getting him to buy into a different offensive identity or accept a reduced role requires exceptional persuasion.

There are many reasons why Harden doesn't have an NBA championship, and while a lot of them come down to bad luck and circumstances, his style of play has to be one of them.

articles.title: Kansas guard Melvin Council breaks foot in practice, likely out until Big 12 slate
articles.summary: Kansas head coach Bill Self is "hopeful" that Melvin Council can return to the court around the start of their conference schedule in January.
articles.body:
The Jayhawks will be without Melvin Council Jr. for at least the next several weeks.

Council broke his right foot in practice on Monday, No. 15 Kansas head coach Bill Self announced . He is set to undergo surgery in the next few days. While Self didn't provide a specific timeline for Council's return, he said they were "hopeful" he'd make it back onto the court around the start of their Big 12 slate.

If that is the case, Council would presumably return in early January. Kansas will open Big 12 play against West Virginia on Jan. 2.

Council averaged 12.7 points and five rebounds per game last season, his first in Lawrence after transferring in from St. Bonaventure. They went 24-11 last year and reached the second round of the NCAA tournament, which marked their fourth straight exit in the opening weekend of the event.

The 24-year-old was granted a preliminary injunction in October, which allowed him to return to play a seventh season of college basketball and return to Kansas for another year. Council had 10 points and seven assists in their 30-point blowout win over Fordham to open the season, and he had six points in their win over Middle Tennessee State on Friday.

While it doesn't sound like Council will be sidelined for too long, the Jayhawks will have to take on several notable opponents without him. They will go up against No. 24 Kentucky at the United Center on Tuesday night, which is part of the "State Farm Champions Classic" in Chicago. They also have Missouri, No. 4 UConn and Ohio State on the schedule before the end of the calendar year, and potentially a battle with No. 1 Florida in the Players Era Eight tournament in Las Vegas later this month.
